name: Vertical B2B deck / sales-collateral automation
rationale: The evaluated broad hypothesis and core initial ICP (B2B SaaS account executives) fail multiple Stage 1 gates and are directly contradicted on fundamental assumptions. First, modern B2B sales reps and leadership report actively abandoning sales decks in favor of live software walk-throughs and conversational discovery (ev-skp-ae-ditching-decks, ev-pain-head-of-sales-deprecating-decks, ev-pain-rep-disdain-for-decks). Second, where sales decks remain in use, disciplined 10-slide master templates reduce per-opportunity customization to 10-15 minutes (ev-pain-master-template-workaround), prompting practitioners to explicitly refuse recurring SaaS subscriptions in favor of one-time master template purchases (ev-wtp-contradiction-manual-template-pushback). Third, Microsoft 365 Copilot directly targets the hypothesized differentiator by embedding file-to-deck generation and corporate .potx brand templates natively into PowerPoint at $23.50-$30/user/mo (ev-skp-m365-copilot-ppt-features, ev-skp-m365-copilot-brand-templates, ev-skp-m365-copilot-pricing), capping standalone willingness to pay well below the founder's $100+/mo ARPU constraint. Fourth, enterprise sales enablement is comprehensively served by entrenched platforms (Seismic LiveDocs, Highspot AutoDocs) where enablement heads enforce template lockdowns to prevent rep autonomy (ev-skp-enablement-brand-lockdown), while CRM integration triggers prohibitive 4.2-week security and SOC 2 procurement hurdles (ev-skp-infosec-procurement-hurdles). Fifth, commercial real estate is monopolized by Buildout Showcase across 50,000+ brokers (ev-skp-buildout-cre-suite), while institutional lenders ignore narrative slide decks (ev-wtp-contradiction-cre-om-skepticism). Sixth, Gate 1 (6 supporting verified pain signals vs. 20 required) and Gate 5 (0 verified reachability records, LOW confidence) fail their required thresholds. Recalculation across all six declared candidate ICPs demonstrates that none can pass independently without pooling unrelated segments. Stage 2 customer prospect mining and interviews are not authorized.

evaluated_scope.hypothesis: B2B teams that regularly create customer-specific sales decks spend meaningful recurring time adapting PowerPoint presentations to individual opportunities. Existing presentation AI tools do not fully solve the workflow because teams require company-specific templates, trusted source material, accurate client customization, and reliably editable native PPTX output. A sufficiently painful segment can justify a B2B SaaS price materially above low-cost consumer presentation subscriptions.
evaluated_scope.founder_model: solo technical founder with coding/research agents
mvp_constraints: buildable by solo technical founder with coding/research agents
exclusions: heavily regulated workflows requiring substantial compliance work before pilot

scope_integrity_notes: All six Stage 1 gates were strictly evaluated on canonical records marked VERIFIED by the Evidence Auditor. In compliance with Stage 1 scope integrity, each candidate ICP was evaluated independently on evidence directly attributable to that specific segment without pooling pain, spend, reachability, or substitute observations across disparate categories. Broad presentation software evidence (such as Gamma, Beautiful.ai, and general Copilot reviews) was restricted to evaluating the broad software gap (G4) and broad scope, and was not attributed to narrow candidate segments.

strongest_positive_evidence.impact: Direct buyer-side commercial real estate broker comment verifies actual contractor spend ($1,000 upfront template and $100 per listing for manual plug-and-play slide completion).
First-hand RevOps practitioner confirms recurring manual time spent assembling customer-facing slides from Salesforce fields, citing the 6-figure pricing barrier of enterprise alternatives.
Verified Trustpilot subscriber review confirms swiping a credit card for AI deck generation and immediately churning due to lack of editable PowerPoint export.
Verified Trustpilot user review directly confirms Gamma completely disregards uploaded PowerPoint templates, generating cluttered, unusable off-brand layouts.
Verified Trustpilot user review confirms exporting presentations to PowerPoint outside smart templates breaks formatting and forces 3x more manual labor than native PowerPoint.

strongest_negative_evidence.impact: Microsoft natively integrates Copilot into PowerPoint to support corporate .potx templates and Brand Kits, learning layout structure and hierarchy from template placeholders.
Microsoft Copilot natively generates complete multi-slide presentations directly from structured Word documents inside PowerPoint.
Microsoft anchors bundled Office AI pricing at $23.50-$30/user/month, capping standalone willingness to pay far below the $100+/month ARPU target.
Buildout Showcase already automates proposals, pitch decks, and Offering Memorandums from property data for 50,000+ CRE brokers.
Seismic LiveDocs already automates pitch decks from Salesforce data into PowerPoint templates for enterprise and mid-market revenue teams.
Sales leadership confirms a disciplined 10-slide master PowerPoint template reduces per-opportunity customization to 10-15 minutes, eliminating the need for dedicated software.
Sales practitioner directly advises against subscribing to AI presentation tools, recommending paying once for a master template and manually customizing details per opportunity.
Sales reps actively abandon pitch decks in favor of live discovery and interactive software walk-throughs to avoid canned pitch perception.
Connecting sales software to CRM and customer notes triggers average 4.2-week enterprise security reviews, SOC 2 Type II, and zero data retention mandates.

top_unknowns: Rate of feature improvements in Microsoft 365 Copilot for PowerPoint regarding custom SharePoint template ingestion in desktop apps.
Whether non-sales B2B workflows (such as recurring PMO reporting or IT MSP QBR reviews) possess sufficient independent willingness to pay to support a pivot.
